method: Three Luna Max grouped source audits with bounded critic passes; not 26 independent skill audits.
verdict: No final source or full-platform completion signoff. Preserve core architecture; stabilize the concurrent tree and close targeted defects before baselining paid E2E. Paid-alpha commercial acceptance remains incomplete.

findings.title: Formance reservation uncertainty bypasses the automatic reconciliation queue
findings.evidence: markReservationUnknown patches Formance and Call reconciliation-required state plus reconciliation evidence but does not set reconciliation. Callers use it for reservation-attach conflict or outcome_unknown; the initializer sets automatic nextAttemptAt only through separate reconciliation wrappers. The due-candidate index requires reconciliation.nextAttemptAt and the worker consumes that query.
findings.consequence: An ambiguous Formance reservation or attach can remain visibly reconciliation-required while the automatic sweep cannot select it, leaving funds held and recovery manual.
findings.recommendation: Initialize reconciliation atomically in this transition or route through the initializer while preserving evidence/reason; add a due-candidate regression test.
findings.tradeoff: Adds one small write and keeps rare uncertainty on the bounded automatic path.

findings.title: Paid Call and recovery HTTP surface has no rate-limit admission
findings.evidence: Current-tree recheck: Call, quote, Call list/status/cancel/reconcile route handlers still directly invoke call-api handlers. Current src/start.ts:101-112 has no rate-limit admission. The available layers remain withHttpRateLimit in src/lib/server/rate-limit.ts:96-105, policy definitions in src/modules/security/rate-limit-policy.ts:34-46,53-70, and Convex rateLimit:admitHttp mutations in convex/rateLimit.ts:33-59, but none is invoked by these routes; src/routes/api.v1.registry.ts remains the existing wrapper pattern. Source-write admission signs commands but does not consume an HTTP bucket. The lower Convex policy at convex/lib/callLifecycle/admission.ts:418-444 governs call reservation budget/spend, not HTTP request rate, and does not cover quote, status/list, cancel, or reconcile traffic.
findings.consequence: A valid credential can repeatedly drive quote/call/status/list/cancel/reconcile work outside the intended public-mutation/public-read HTTP budget, increasing abuse, cost, queue pressure, and recovery churn. The separate call budget does not provide request-rate control.
findings.recommendation: Wrap route handlers with explicit public-mutation/public-read admission and add 429/header route tests.
findings.tradeoff: Adds one admission round trip per request and requires policy-specific route tests.

findings.title: Tool discovery freshness is sourced from the wrong projection
findings.evidence: List/search freshness and cursor scope use latestReconcileBusinessSupplyProjectionsCompletion, described as registrySearchDocuments, but the current source path calls capabilityToolCatalog:search, which delegates to capabilitySupplyTools.search and current capabilityPublications at capabilitySupplyToolQueries.ts:304-353. workloadCron.ts:483-486 invokes a rebuild that reads publications and writes only registrySearchDocuments at capabilitySupplyProjection.ts:250-302.
findings.consequence: A successful current publication search can be labelled absent/stale, and a business-only rebuild changes the cursor scope without changing the Tool rows, so a subsequent page is rejected as a foreign/stale cursor; clients may retry or reject valid pages.
findings.recommendation: Track a real publication/Tool-catalog generation/completion signal, or remove freshness/cursor coupling until one exists; correct the comment and add a contract test.
findings.tradeoff: Generation metadata costs a small write/read; removing the field changes the public cursor/response contract but is simpler. No economic migration.

findings.title: Receipt Complete label is ambiguous when payment is unresolved
findings.evidence: Any result.kind=completed sets complete=true and maps every progress stage to complete (121-136,173-200), while usage.chargeState=outcome_unknown makes purchaseStatusLabel return Open — outcome uncertain (144-158). issueFromFound returns no warning for completed output (214-228). The route uses complete for the success badge and reuse actions (src/routes/calls.$callRef.tsx:297,318-344). The test explicitly codifies the contradiction at tests/unit/capability-execution/call-receipt-view.test.ts:152-179. Run again is explicitly a fresh purchase with a new idempotency key and terms check (src/routes/calls.$callRef.tsx:500-519), so the source does not prove an unsafe retry.
findings.consequence: Complete may intentionally mean output delivery, but the copy does not say so; all stages appear complete while settlement says uncertain. A buyer must reconcile contradictory statuses and may treat the commercial purchase as terminal.
findings.recommendation: Choose and label the semantics: use Output available when delivery is complete but payment is unresolved, and Purchase resolved only after the commercial state is resolved. Mark settlement/complete stages as attention for unknown outcomes and add a clear fresh-purchase/reconciliation warning around Run again; do not blanket-disable a new Call without an explicit authority/risk decision.
findings.tradeoff: Requires a small projector/copy/test change rather than a new execution object; it preserves useful output and the explicit fresh-purchase path while removing the false-terminal ambiguity.

findings.title: Committed Quote commercial scope is a known paid-alpha gap
findings.evidence: The committed result contains Tool/version/input, AUD price, Account/balance, budget, policy refs, evidenceDigest and continuation (114-148). PRODUCT.md:340-352 explicitly documents that the current DTO does not yet establish explicit Provider/Seller fields or complete principal-reseller terms; START_LINE.md:53-61 states those facts are required for the full start-line proof, and docs/glossary.md:19-22 defines them as Quote semantics. The focused current-tool quote test (tests/unit/capability-execution/current-tool-quote.test.ts:82-120) protects readiness/price/effects/provider-authority drift. This is an accepted, documented scope gap, not a newly discovered source defect.
findings.consequence: The current source contract cannot prove the complete commercial choice before paid-alpha; a source-level E2E run can still exercise the accepted current Quote/Call path if this limitation is explicit.
findings.recommendation: Treat this as a before-paid-alpha acceptance item: extend the persisted and returned Quote with structured Provider/Seller refs plus terms, data-use/effects, unknowns, retry and challenge evidence, and expose the same packet through HTTP/MCP/CLI. Do not make the known gap a blocker to beginning source/preview E2E unless the release contract says those fields are required for that run.
findings.tradeoff: Adds contract and fixture migration and some response size, but avoids a second competing decision object and keeps the accepted one-Quote path.

findings.title: Derived Purchase resolution needs a stable cross-surface acceptance contract
findings.evidence: The source explicitly says purchaseStatusLabel is presentation only (140-143), which is permitted by the product boundary. CallReceipt in src/modules/capability-execution/call-contracts.ts:173-224 carries payment/refund/obligation facts, while README.md:60-64 records the complete Seller/Provider-obligation/tax/business evidence as an open milestone. P-2 supplies the concrete cross-surface example: the same input can project Complete and Open — outcome uncertain.
findings.consequence: Without one named derived-resolution contract and its state-combination tests, receipt, activity and agent responses can explain the same Call differently; the existing mixed state is already hard to interpret.
findings.recommendation: Specify and test one canonical derived Purchase-resolution projection across receipt, activity and agent responses, keeping Call as the execution identity and leaving storage/identity choice open. Add a durable record only if later evidence shows the derivation cannot remain consistent.
findings.tradeoff: Requires contract and acceptance-test work without committing to a new table or second market object.
skills_principles: iceinvein-design-review: complete the core chain before accretion

findings.title: Owner cannot see per-Agent remaining spend with Account spend
findings.evidence: Activity renders Account-wide Calls, reconciliation count and Account spend only (181-203). Agent detail shows per-call/daily/monthly ceilings and settled charges/coverage (src/components/ae/console/AeAgentOperatorConsole.tsx:486-511), while Credit shows only Account balance (src/components/ae/console/AeOwnerCredit.tsx:131-163). The maintained scoreboard marks the expectation absent at docs/workflow/simple-user-expectations.md:14.
findings.consequence: The owner must mentally join separate pages to answer whether a particular Agent can still spend; this misses START_LINE.md:91-95's customer-visible spend-by-Agent proof and weakens safe authority management.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-Agent used, reserved, remaining and coverage state to the Activity or Agents surface, linked to the exact spending policy and Account balance. Keep unavailable amounts explicit.
findings.tradeoff: Needs a read-model/query join and careful reservation semantics, but does not require a new funding or authority concept.

findings.title: Customer remedy request stops at email support
findings.evidence: Automatic release/refund states are projected in convex/capabilityCallProjection.ts:790-808 and displayed in the receipt, but the inspected customer routes contain no refund/remedy request action; Help offers email, Call lookup and listing correction (39-85). The tracked scoreboard marks “Ask for a refund” absent at docs/workflow/simple-user-expectations.md:17-19.
findings.consequence: When delivery is invalid or a paid outcome needs a customer remedy, the owner has no idempotent case tied to the Call and must initiate an unstructured support exchange.
findings.recommendation: Add an eligibility-gated Request remedy action on the Call receipt that creates one idempotent case reference, captures the selected reason and evidence pointer, and exposes pending/accepted/declined resolution status without exposing treasury internals.
findings.tradeoff: Adds support triage and legal-policy workflow; it can remain narrow to Call-linked refunds/remedies rather than a general dispute system.
skills_principles: iceinvein-design-review: close the core delivery-to-remedy chain

findings.title: Team authority scope is a product decision, not a completed journey
findings.evidence: The active start line scopes one Customer/Account and one durable Agent (START_LINE.md:167-170). Generic membership storage and guarded add/end operations exist (src/modules/principal-account/account/registry.ts:375-445), but owner settings expose Profile, sign-out, compromise recovery and security history only (owner.settings.tsx:10-43; OwnerSettingsSections.tsx:14-36).
findings.consequence: If alpha implies a business team, no owner can invite, inspect or revoke a member's Account authority; if alpha is intentionally single-owner, continuing to imply team authority will create an avoidable expectation gap.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document the alpha principal: either state single-owner Account explicitly, or add a narrow membership page with invite, role/scope, revoke and audit evidence before inviting teams.
findings.tradeoff: A single-owner decision preserves the current milestone; membership UI adds identity/recovery and policy complexity that should not be smuggled into E2E.
skills_principles: bounded-context-auditor: distinguish generic Membership from Customer/Agent roles

findings.title: Hosted and installed agent proof is a next alpha validation
findings.evidence: README explicitly separates source acceptance from hosted deployment and installed-package compatibility (50-52), says CLI compatibility remains pending (75-76), and says loopback can prove discovery/connect/funding but Quote/Call require a public HTTPS origin with credentials (165-166). The machine quickstart repeats that it is not hosted/package acceptance (202-218). No runtime/browser/package/MCP-client checks were permitted in this audit.
findings.consequence: Alpha cannot claim the paid journey across the hosted and distributed agent surfaces until the subsequent validation is run; this is not a blocker to beginning source or preview E2E.
findings.recommendation: After the E2E harness exists, run one hosted HTTPS funding/Quote/Call/recovery canary and an installed CLI/authenticated MCP parity check. Record the origin, package revision and exact result references as the next alpha release gate.
findings.tradeoff: Needs hosted credentials and external x402/testnet setup, but is the smallest proof that the claimed customer path exists outside source fixtures.
findings.synthesis_note: Subsequent validation explicitly excluded from this audit, not a defect or prerequisite to beginning all E2E.

findings.title: Provider-obligation projection has competing writers
findings.evidence: Money obligation dispute/reversal/resolution mutations patch both moneyProviderObligations and capabilityCallProjections. dispatch.ts:984-997,999-1046 independently reads the obligation and writes the duplicated provider fields; convex-schema.ts:287-318 stores them on the call projection.
findings.consequence: Convex makes the inspected mutations transactional and no current stale ordering was demonstrated, but every money path must maintain a second table; future paths can leave economic status views inconsistent or be overwritten by a later rebuild.
findings.recommendation: Give the call projection owner a typed internal obligation-state command, or derive provider state from the obligation source at read time and remove the duplicate field. Preserve its distinction from Charge, delivery and settlement.
findings.tradeoff: A directed command preserves indexed reads but adds a cross-domain call; read derivation reduces writers but adds join/read cost. Schema migration is avoidable.
findings.synthesis_note: No current stale state or transaction race was established; transactional writes and rebuild readback work. Clarify ownership during related work; not an alpha gate by itself.

findings.title: MoneyQueryPort couples unrelated read roles and advertises unsupported methods
findings.evidence: The public port combines credit, activity, key usage, Provider earnings and payout status while importing Convex PaginationOptions. action-execution needs only key usage; money-query.ts:39-84 throws unsupported for earnings/payout and tests provide throwing stubs at execution-public.test.ts:118-134.
findings.consequence: Callers and adapters depend on unrelated roles and unsupported capabilities fail late, increasing change amplification as Provider console work grows.
findings.recommendation: Split usage, customer-credit, and Provider-payout/earnings query ports; compose adapters and keep framework pagination types at the server boundary.
findings.tradeoff: Typed adapter migration; no data or commercial meaning change, so defer unless unsupported paths activate.

findings.title: Capability-supply public barrel is an internal dependency hub
findings.evidence: The public barrel exports transport/importer/Convex schema/graph/ledger/publication implementations; internal publication/draft.ts:8-21 and internal/tool-project.ts:1-15 import that barrel. dependency-cruiser.cjs:63-82 and 91-105 record accepted intra-module cycles.
findings.consequence: Internal changes can re-enter through the public hub, obscuring ownership and amplifying bundling/codegen risk across supply publication code; no current runtime malfunction was established.
findings.recommendation: Extract stable refs, value types and wire contracts into leaf modules; invert internal imports to those leaves and keep implementations private, then lower the ratchet after graph proof.
findings.tradeoff: A bounded supply import migration and generated-output review; no product or stored-data change.

findings.title: Call worker crosses the stated thin Convex host boundary
findings.evidence: The Node worker surface imports generated ActionCtx and worker internals; convex/capabilityCallWorker.ts:7-17,95-103 imports and invokes it, while runPreparation.ts:44-52 and runRelease.ts:14-18 import generated internal/ActionCtx and concrete Convex projections.
findings.consequence: Convex generated API/runtime changes ripple through execution workers and make standalone worker tests host-aware; no current runtime malfunction was established.
findings.recommendation: Move Convex-bound orchestration/adapters behind a Convex host boundary or plain CallWorkerContext port; retain createCallApplication and lifecycle contracts in src/modules.
findings.tradeoff: Import and Convex-specific test migration without schema or public-contract migration.

findings.title: Safe seller-canary proof has a potential unbounded-history scaling path
findings.evidence: safeBeforeReleaseSellerCanaryRefusal queries actionExecutionAttempts by executionRef and calls collect(), then sorts and validates the full history; the canonical attempt reader uses bounded take().
findings.consequence: If retry/re-arm policy permits attempt histories beyond Convex read/return/transaction limits, the proof can fail or degrade and strand a valid safe call in manual recovery. This audit did not establish that reachable growth is currently unbounded.
findings.recommendation: Bound or paginate proof history and persist a digest/count invariant; fail closed when incomplete.
findings.tradeoff: Very long histories may move to manual review under a strict cap.

findings.title: Notification and hosted support inbox surfaces are known later scope
findings.evidence: The scoreboard marks notifications absent for Buyer and Provider and says Package 7 owns the hosted support inbox. The current Help page provides status links, email and a public developer issue path (src/routes/support.tsx:47-85).
findings.consequence: Users must poll Calls or email support for changes; this is a full-platform gap when promised, but it is not an active start-line defect.
findings.recommendation: Keep this deferred and state the alpha support/notification promise precisely. If proactive events enter alpha, define event ownership, delivery/retry and an in-product history before adding channel chrome.
findings.tradeoff: Deferral keeps the managed Call spine small; adding it early introduces durable event and delivery policy work.

findings.title: Operator has no joined queue for stuck commercial work
findings.evidence: The maintained operator scoreboard explicitly marks a joined view of what is stuck absent. Catalog health and audit remain separate panels (src/routes/_operator/admin.index-health.tsx:85-100; src/routes/_operator/admin.audit-events.tsx:45-55), while Provider Tools has only its local attention count (src/components/ae/offerings/AeProviderWorkspace.tsx:269-280).
findings.consequence: An operator must correlate Catalog, Call/reconciliation, Provider readiness and payout facts manually when resolving an incident.
findings.recommendation: Add a later operator read model joining case type, affected Account/Call/Tool, current owner, next safe action and evidence reference. Keep domain records separate underneath.
findings.tradeoff: Improves operations after start-line evidence exists, but adds a cross-domain projection that should follow measured support volume.

limitations: Source audit only; no browser, hosted, deployment, live-money or installed-client proof.
Current checkout changed during the audit and final checks; no immutable tested revision.
Source findings were scrutinized but no exhaustive line-by-line or formal security/compliance assurance is claimed.
No source fixes, rollback, commits or external actions performed by this audit.
